subject: Hosted API response suppression — customer advisory & post-incident follow-up
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@terrabio.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: unexpected empty responses from hosted API

Marissa —

We started seeing a spike of ~10–15% of POST /v1/generate requests returning empty/zero-token responses starting at ~08:45 PST. The requests were identical to successful ones earlier in the morning. This is affecting our UI where user prompts render as blank. No 5xx status codes, just a 200 with no generated text.

Sample request IDs we collected: rb-req-94a1, rb-req-94b6, rb-req-94d0.

Can you confirm if this is on Redwood's side or something we changed? We're blocked for a subset of users.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Senior Product Manager — TerraBio

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@terrabio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: unexpected empty responses from hosted API

Hi Elena — thank you for the fast heads up and the sample request IDs.

We opened an ops bridge and are investigating now. Initial triage from the runtime team shows an anomalous "response-suppression" signal that can cause the token generator to exit early when concurrent prefix-cache invalidations align with certain batching windows. That said, we'll validate with logs for the request IDs you provided.

Immediate next steps (what we'll do now):
- Pull full request/response traces for rb-req-94a1, rb-req-94b6, rb-req-94d0.
- Temporarily widen batching windows for TerraBio traffic and disable aggressive prefix invalidation for affected pools.
- Notify you when we have a mitigation live.

Can you share whether these requests were using streaming and whether you had any custom truncation tokens in prompts? Any tiny detail helps.

Apologies for the interruption — we'll prioritize this.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0113

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@terrabio.com>, TerraBio Support <ops@terrabio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 11:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Hosted API — interim advisory & status page link (impact reduced)

Elena / TerraBio —

Quick update from the bridge: we identified a narrow window where concurrent prefix cache invalidations + a rare batching timing lead to the generator returning zero tokens for some requests. We rolled two mitigations at 10:05 PST:

1) Disabled aggressive prefix invalidation for TerraBio's customer pool (reduces race window).
2) Adjusted batching thresholds so affected requests route to a stability-optimized path.

Impact: successful request rate for your traffic improved from ~88–90% up to ~99% after the changes. We have been monitoring for ~60 minutes and are seeing normal behavior.

We've published an incident note on our status page with a brief timeline and ongoing monitoring: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2028-02-response-suppression (public).

Attachments: incident_dashboard.png (ops dashboard screenshot), redwood_status_log_2028-02-14.txt (sanitized trace snippets).

Action for you: please confirm whether the clients that were seeing blanks are back to normal. If you still have samples, send them and we'll prioritize.

Sorry again for the disruption — if you want, we can schedule a short post-incident call tomorrow to walk through root cause and safeguards.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@terrabio.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 17:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API response suppression — internal summary & next steps

Folks —

Summary of the incident (post-incident notes):
- Timeline: 08:45 PST anomalous empty responses observed by TerraBio. Ops bridge opened 09:00. Mitigations deployed 10:05. Monitoring confirmed recovery by 11:05.
- Root cause: a rare timing interaction between prefix cache eviction logic and the continuous-batching scheduler that allowed the token generator to skip decode cycles when a request's KV cache was invalidated mid-batch. This manifests as 200 OK with zero tokens.
- Scope: customer-visible for ~2% of hosts across a small number of high-concurrency customers; TerraBio experienced ~10–15% locally due to traffic profile.

Immediate follow-ups (actions already in flight):
1) Revert aggressive prefix invalidation globally for affected pools until we ship a race-free invalidation routine (engineers: runtime-team). ETA: 72 hours for rollout.
2) Add a defensive check in the generator pipeline that returns an explicit 5xx/429 (instead of a 200/ zero tokens) when KV cache state is inconsistent. ETA: 2 weeks.
3) Add additional observability: a real-time metric for "token-generation-empty" events and an alert tied to customer error rates. ETA: 48 hours.
4) Customer communications: Marissa, please coordinate a short postmortem email and offer a 30-minute review call.

I've attached sanitized trace snippets to the thread (redwood_status_log_2028-02-14.txt) and included the ops dashboard screenshot for context (incident_dashboard.png).

Markus Klein
VP, Production Engineering — Redwood Inference
